guide.text: These sources are the FY2026 annual report and September 17, 2026 board notes for Thistledown Rides, a sample nonprofit.
Volunteer drivers give older adults in Marrow County free rides to medical visits, and they gave 4,312 one-way rides this year.
The group could not fill 538 ride requests, about one in nine, and dialysis rides are the hardest to cover.
Spending was $164,800 and income was $171,200, and each one-way ride cost about $38.
The board will ask the Fallow Creek Foundation for $62,000 a year for two years to pay for a full-time ride coordinator.

asks.what: A short deck for the Fallow Creek Foundation's site visit

brief.who: Fallow Creek Foundation site visit staff
brief.goal: Fund $62,000 a year for two years for a ride coordinator

questions.text: A coordinator would fill about 300 of the 538 turned-down requests, so 238 stay unfilled. With only a $6,400 surplus, how will the January rise on the $18,900 insurance bill get covered?
Two of the 31 dialysis riders were hospitalized after missed treatments, but nobody knows if a ride was the cause. Should the deck use that fact at all?
Each ride costs about $38, and the county grant already gives $72,000. How will the deck show that the $62,000 yearly ask is not the whole budget?

brief.goal: Fund $62,000 a year for two years for a ride coordinator

case: We turned away 538 ride requests in FY2026, about one in nine, and older adults in Marrow County miss medical care without a ride. We ask the Fallow Creek Foundation for $62,000 a year for two years to fund a full-time ride coordinator. Staff estimate the coordinator could fill about 300 more requests a year.

argument.reader: Fallow Creek Foundation staff at the site visit, who decide whether to fund a full-time ride coordinator at $62,000 a year for two years.

instructions.said: lead with the riders we turn away, not with how many rides we give.

lead.heading: We turned away 538 ride requests last year, about one in nine

evidence.text: We could not fill 538 ride requests in FY2026, about one in nine.
We gave 4,312 one-way rides in FY2026, up from 3,240 the year before.
Most unfilled requests came less than two days ahead or were for early-morning dialysis.

points.heading: Without a ride, older adults in Marrow County miss medical care

evidence.text: 84 percent of 212 surveyed riders said they would have missed at least one appointment without Thistledown.
39 percent said they had put off care because they could not get a ride.
The county has no bus outside Kestrel, and a taxi from the hill towns costs about $90 each way.
A Pell Hollow rider wrote: "Before you, I rescheduled my eye surgery twice."

points.heading: Dialysis riders need three early rides a week, and some go unfilled

evidence.text: A dialysis patient needs three rides a week, every week, usually starting before 7 a.m.
We drove 31 dialysis riders this year, and 19 of the 538 unfilled rides were dialysis rides.
When a dialysis ride falls through, the patient pays for a taxi or misses a treatment.
The kidney unit said two of our riders were hospitalized after missed treatments. We do not know whether a ride was the cause.

points.heading: A four-hour ride line and a part-time scheduler cannot keep up

evidence.text: The ride line is open only four hours a day, weekdays 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.
One part-time scheduler answers the line and also matches drivers to rides.
23 of our 71 drivers are over 75, and 14 drivers stopped this year.
We trained 22 new drivers this year to keep up.

points.heading: A full-time coordinator could fill about 300 more requests a year

evidence.text: Today the scheduler job is half-time; the plan makes it a full-time ride coordinator.
Today the line is open 9 to 1; the plan keeps it open 9 to 5.
The coordinator would recruit and schedule a standing team of dialysis drivers.
Staff estimate the coordinator could fill about 300 more requests a year. This is a staff estimate.

counter.objection: Are we being asked to pay for your whole program?
counter.heading: Others already fund most rides; this grant pays for one role

evidence.text: Each one-way ride cost us about $38.
The county's Area Agency on Aging grant already gives $72,000 of our $164,800 spending.
Two foundation grants gave $48,000, church and individual gifts $38,700, and United Way $12,500.
Income was $171,200 against spending of $164,800 in FY2026.

ask.heading: Fund a full-time ride coordinator at $62,000 a year for two years
buys: A full-time ride coordinator, turning the half-time scheduler job into a full-time one
A ride line open 9 to 5 on weekdays
A standing team of dialysis drivers, recruited and scheduled by the coordinator
ask.rest: The county Area Agency on Aging grant ($72,000), two foundation grants ($48,000), church and individual gifts ($38,700) and United Way ($12,500) fund the rest of the work. The sources do not say what happens after the grant.

P9.text:
THISTLEDOWN RIDES (SAMPLE). BOARD MEETING NOTES, SEPTEMBER 17, 2026
Sample notes. Fictional organization and people.

P10.text:
Present: Rev. Augustin Malloy-Fenn (chair), Teodora Quist (treasurer), Odalys Venn-Carraway (director), Hollis
Aberkrombie (scheduler), four board members.

P11.text:
1. Treasurer. Year closed with a small surplus. Reserve is about two months of spending. Teodora: the insurance
 carrier has told us our premium will go up in January. We don't have the number yet. Not for outside use.

P12.text: 2. Driver recognition dinner set for November 8.

P13.text:
3. The ask. The board agreed to ask the Fallow Creek Foundation for $62,000 a year for two years for a full-time
 ride coordinator, which turns Hollis's half-time job into a full-time one and keeps the ride line open 9 to 5.
 Application due December 1.
 - Odalys to make a short deck for the foundation's site visit. No more than eight slides.
 - Augustin: lead with the riders we turn away, not with how many rides we give.
 - Teodora: show what one ride costs and what the county grant already covers, so they see this is not our whole
 budget.
 - Hollis: be careful with the two hospitalizations. Say we don't know a missed ride was the cause, or leave them out.
 - Augustin: the 300 more rides is a staff estimate. Say so.

P1.text:
*Sample organization. Thistledown Rides, Marrow County, and every person named here are fictional.*
Fiscal year July 2025 to June 2026. Prepared by staff for members, riders, drivers and the board.

P2.text:
Thistledown Rides gives older adults in Marrow County free rides to medical appointments. A rider calls our office at
least two days ahead, a trained volunteer driver picks them up at home in their own car, waits during the visit, and
brings them home. Riders must be 65 or older or have a disability that keeps them from driving. Most of our riders
live alone. The county has no bus service outside the town of Kestrel, and a taxi from the hill towns to the regional
hospital in Kestrel costs about $90 each way.
We began in 2017 with eight drivers from two churches. Today our staff is a director, Odalys Venn-Carraway, and a
part-time scheduler, Hollis Aberkrombie, who answers the ride line on weekdays from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.

P3.text:
- **Rides.** We gave 4,312 one-way rides, up from 3,240 the year before.
- **Riders.** 486 different riders used the service, up from 401.
- **Drivers.** 71 active volunteer drivers gave 9,640 hours and drove about 118,000 miles.
- **Appointments.** 61 percent of rides were to primary care or specialist visits, 22 percent to dialysis or cancer
 treatment, and the rest to physical therapy, eye care and the pharmacy.
- **Turned down.** We could not fill 538 ride requests, about one in nine. Most were requests made less than two days
 ahead, or for early-morning dialysis, when few drivers are free.

P4.text:
In our April 2026 rider survey (212 riders answered), 84 percent said they would have missed at least one appointment
in the past year without Thistledown. 39 percent said they had put off care because they could not get a ride before
they found us. One rider from Pell Hollow wrote: "My daughter lives four hours away. Before you, I rescheduled my eye
surgery twice."

P5.text:
Dialysis is the hardest need to meet. A dialysis patient needs three rides a week, every week, usually starting before
7 a.m. We drove 31 dialysis riders this year, and 19 of the 538 rides we could not fill were dialysis rides. When a
dialysis ride falls through, the patient either pays for a taxi or misses a treatment. The regional hospital's kidney
unit told us that two of our riders were hospitalized after missed treatments this year. We do not know whether a ride
was the cause.

P6.text:
Our drivers are mostly retired, and 23 of the 71 are over 75 themselves. Fourteen drivers stopped this year, most
for their own health. We trained 22 new drivers. Every driver passes a background check and a driving-record check
and takes a two-hour safety course. Drivers are paid back 45 cents a mile for gas if they ask; about half do.

P7.text:
FY2026 spending was $164,800: staff $98,500, mileage paid back to drivers $26,600, insurance $18,900, background checks
and training $7,200, phone and scheduling software $6,400, and office costs $7,200.
Income was $171,200: the county's Area Agency on Aging grant $72,000, two foundation grants $48,000, church and
individual gifts $38,700, and a United Way grant of $12,500. Riders pay nothing. Each one-way ride cost us about
$38.

P8.text:
The ride line is open only four hours a day, and Hollis is also the person who matches drivers to rides. Staff
estimate that a full-time ride coordinator could fill about 300 more requests a year, mostly by recruiting and
scheduling a standing team of dialysis drivers and by keeping the line open until 5 p.m. The board has asked staff
to find the funding before the county's grant cycle in spring.
